item.description:
Note:
  • Pace history restarts once with this update. A card returns to "Learning history" and rebuilds unless its provider gives TokenBar a stable account identifier, which today means Codex with an account ID on its credential, and the Antigravity IDE. This is the cost of the identity fix below and it happens only once.
Fixes:
  • Pace history no longer restarts every time another app refreshes a shared login. Providers without a stable account identifier kept losing their learned usage curve whenever the Claude CLI or a sibling tool rotated the credential they share, so Historical pace could never accumulate.
  • A pace marker in deficit is now highlighted whether it came from the historical curve or the linear estimate. Previously only a historical result was coloured, so the warning appeared and disappeared as the fit requalified while the deficit itself never moved.
  • A clock disagreement no longer discards the whole quota history. A single forward jump of the system clock, from a time sync or a sleep and wake, could leave one window with a timestamp ahead of the next read, which quarantined every provider's history at once. It is now repaired in place, and only genuinely unverifiable data is dropped.
Improved:
  • Updater: the bundled Sparkle framework is now compiled from source as part of the build.

Fixes:
  • The Discord agent picker no longer lists every agent TokenBar recognises. It used to offer a row for each one, including agents you had never run and agents you had hidden, and naming one of those left the presence empty without saying why.

New:
  • TokenBar can publish what you are working on to Discord. It is off by default. You choose which of today's tokens, the agent and the cost band it shows, and which agent by name; all three are shown unless you change them.
  • A Usage attribution page in Settings lets you declare which subscription a client's local usage belongs to. Running another provider's model through an agent is common, and the usage was previously drawn against that agent's own quota. Stats now breaks the total into assigned, excluded and undeclared.
Improved:
  • Opening the popover no longer waits for two extra scans. The chart runs on its own and appears as soon as it is ready.
  • Scanning is faster: on an 8 GB history, a cold scan dropped about 31 percent and a warm scan about 37 percent. Peak memory is about 15 percent higher, which is the trade for the parallel parsing.
  • Restarting shows your last dashboard immediately and refreshes behind it, instead of showing nothing for several seconds.
  • Turns that an in-place transcript rewrite used to drop are now kept. This does not restore history already lost. A total can still fall on the first launch if a transcript was compacted since the last scan, because the rebuild reads the file as it stands now.
Fixes:
  • Inactive segments of the view switch are clickable again.
  • Codex shows its monochrome mark instead of the ChatGPT green.
  • Hovering a heatmap cell rings it, the way the bar chart already did.

Note: the first launch after this update rescans every client once, because the engine's cache format changed. Later launches are back to normal.

Thanks: @yeha98555

New:
  • A flat contribution heatmap joins the bar and 3D views in the usage chart. Press Command-G to cycle through all three.
  • Claude plans that report per-model weekly caps now show those limits alongside the session and weekly windows.
Improved:
  • Reopening the popover no longer recomputes the hourly views, so they appear right away.
  • The turn count shows a loading state instead of looking empty while it is still being read.
Fixes:
  • Non-square menu-bar animation art, such as the parrot, is fitted to the bar instead of being stretched to a square.

New:
  • Daily and Monthly usage now show Codex and Claude turn counts alongside message totals, making human interactions easier to distinguish from agent and tool-loop activity.
Fixes:
  • Message-only activity remains visible in Daily and Monthly history, drill-downs, active-day counts, streaks, and year visibility without distorting token or cost charts.

New:
  • Brand logos for the Cline, jcode, MiMo Code, and gjc tabs, instead of a letter badge.
Improved:
  • The client-tab row now scrolls with a plain vertical mouse wheel, so a mouse without a horizontal-scroll wheel can reach every tab.
Fixes:
  • Antigravity CLI now shows the shared Antigravity quota instead of an empty or duplicate limit card.

New:
  • Tracks five more local AI coding tools: Cline, Antigravity CLI, jcode, MiMo Code, and gjc.
Improved:
  • More accurate cost and per-tool attribution across AI token usage.
  • Corrected Codex usage counts for forked and sub-agent sessions.
  • Antigravity CLI usage is now dated per turn, so the live view and daily totals reflect when each turn actually happened.
Fixes:
  • The app no longer crashes if the usage parser hits an unexpected error.
  • More reliable live usage updates, including for the newly added tools.
